description: Made some of the sharpest crime films of the 1940s at RKO before the anti-Communist hearings sent him to prison and then into testimony against former colleagues.

name: René Clément
signature: The versatile craftsman of postwar French cinema.
description: Began in documentary and made the first great French film about the resistance, then literary adaptations and thrillers.

name: Ben Sharpsteen
signature: Supervising director of Disney's Pinocchio and Dumbo.
description: A veteran animator who coordinated Disney's features of the early 1940s and later produced the studio's nature documentaries.

name: Renato Castellani
signature: A founder of pink neorealism: neorealist methods with a lighter heart.
description: His comedies of young love among the poor kept the locations and amateur casts of neorealism and dropped its despair.

name: Teinosuke Kinugasa
signature: A former female-role actor who made Japan's boldest silent film and its first colour success abroad.
description: Started as an onnagata, playing women's roles, and directed for forty years. His work runs from avant-garde experiment to lavish period drama.

name: Delbert Mann
signature: Brought the intimacy of live television drama to the cinema.
description: A leading director of American live television in the 1950s. Marty, about a lonely Bronx butcher, kept the small scale of its television original.

name: Jacques-Yves Cousteau
signature: The oceanographer who took the film camera underwater.
description: A French naval officer and explorer whose films from the research ship Calypso showed audiences the sea floor in colour for the first time.

name: Marcel Camus
signature: Set the Orpheus myth in the Rio carnival.
description: A former assistant to several French directors. Black Orpheus, shot in Rio with a largely amateur Black cast, was a worldwide success.

name: Henri Colpi
signature: An editor of the Left Bank group who directed one prize-winning film about memory.
description: Best known as an editor. His first feature follows a café owner who believes a passing tramp is her husband, deported during the war.

name: Anselmo Duarte
signature: A Brazilian star actor who directed the first South American film to win the Palme d'Or.
description: A matinee idol turned director. His success at Cannes was resented by the younger Cinema Novo directors, who saw his style as old-fashioned.

name: Richard Lester
signature: Gave the Swinging Sixties their film style.
description: An American who made his career in Britain, coming from television and the Goons. His comedies are cut fast, full of visual gags and asides to the camera.

name: Pietro Germi
signature: Moved from neorealist drama to savage comedies of Italian manners.
description: His early films are social dramas set in Sicily. In the 1960s he became the sharpest satirist of Italian codes of honour and marriage.

name: Claude Lelouch
signature: A one-man band who shoots his own films with a roving handheld camera.
description: He produces, writes and photographs romantic films built on chance meetings, music and improvisation.

name: Elio Petri
signature: The most grotesque and furious voice of Italian political cinema.
description: His films turn factory work, policing and power into feverish satire, with Gian Maria Volonté in the lead.

name: Alan Bridges
signature: A British television director with a fine ear for class.
description: He worked mostly in television drama. His few features are restrained period pieces about the English class system.

name: Jerry Schatzberg
signature: A fashion photographer who made three of the quietest films of New Hollywood.
description: His early films observe drifters and addicts with a photographer's patience, on real streets and roads.

name: Mohammed Lakhdar-Hamina
signature: The leading filmmaker of independent Algeria.
description: He joined the Algerian resistance's film unit and later ran the national newsreel office. His films tell the story of colonisation and the war of independence on an epic scale.

name: Paolo & Vittorio Taviani
signature: Brothers who directed alternate scenes and merged history with fable.
description: They began as political documentarists. Their films set peasants and rebels in Italian landscapes and tell their stories with the stylisation of folk tales.

name: Volker Schlöndorff
signature: The New German Cinema's specialist in literary adaptation.
description: He trained in France and brought its craft back to Germany, adapting Musil, Böll, Grass and Proust.

name: Costa-Gavras
signature: Invented the modern political thriller.
description: Born in Greece and based in France. He applies the pace and suspense of the thriller to real cases of state violence.

name: Yılmaz Güney
signature: A Kurdish star and director who made his greatest films from a prison cell.
description: Turkey's most popular screen actor, nicknamed the Ugly King, he turned to directing films about the poor and was jailed repeatedly.

name: Roland Joffé
signature: Made two large-scale dramas of conscience in the 1980s.
description: A British theatre and television director whose first two features set individual moral choices against historical catastrophe.

name: Bille August
signature: A Danish director of patient, novelistic family sagas.
description: Trained as a cinematographer. His best-known films are long, classical adaptations set in nineteenth- and early twentieth-century Scandinavia.

name: Steven Soderbergh
signature: Restlessly alternates between studio entertainments and experiments, usually as his own cameraman.
description: His debut launched the American independent boom of the 1990s. Since then he has treated each film as a new formal problem.

name: Nanni Moretti
signature: Italy's wry diarist, usually playing a version of himself.
description: He writes, directs and stars in comedies about the Italian left, family and his own neuroses.

name: Michael Moore
signature: Made the first-person polemic the most commercially successful kind of documentary.
description: He appears in his own films as a baseball-capped everyman confronting corporations and politicians, mixing archive footage, stunts and satire.

name: Laurent Cantet
signature: Studied work, school and power through workshops with non-professional actors.
description: His films grow out of long improvisation sessions with the people whose world they depict.

name: Abdellatif Kechiche
signature: Films young people in very long scenes of talk and eating, shot in close-up.
description: Born in Tunis and raised in Nice. He shoots enormous amounts of footage to capture unguarded behaviour.

name: Jacques Audiard
signature: Brings art-film intimacy to the French crime genre.
description: A screenwriter's son who started as a writer and editor. His films follow outsiders remaking themselves, in a tactile handheld style.

name: Ruben Östlund
signature: Stages excruciating social embarrassment in long, fixed shots.
description: A Swedish satirist of male pride and privilege who builds each film around a handful of drawn-out set pieces.

name: Julia Ducournau
signature: Makes body horror about transformation and family.
description: A French director whose films treat flesh, metal and appetite with both shock and tenderness.

name: Justine Triet
signature: Dissects couples through talk, argument and courtroom procedure.
description: She began with documentaries and comedies of chaotic domestic life before turning a marriage into a trial.

name: Sean Baker
signature: Films people at the margins of the American economy with energy and warmth.
description: He casts newcomers and non-professionals, shoots on real locations and edits his own films.

name: Andrey Zvyagintsev
signature: Austere moral tragedies of family and state in contemporary Russia.
description: His films set broken families against vast northern landscapes and an indifferent bureaucracy. The compositions are severe and slow, and biblical parallels sit under stories of everyday corruption.

name: Joachim Trier
signature: Literary, melancholy portraits of young adults in Oslo.
description: He writes with Eskil Vogt. Their films use narration, digressions and sudden formal flourishes to follow people stuck between who they are and who they meant to be.

name: Alejandro González Iñárritu
signature: Virtuoso camera work in the service of suffering and redemption.
description: He began with fractured, interlocking stories written with Guillermo Arriaga and moved to films staged as apparently unbroken takes with the cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki.

name: Alejandro Jodorowsky
signature: Mystical, blasphemous visions that invented the midnight movie.
description: A Chilean-born theatre maker, mime and comics writer. His films are allegorical quests full of tarot symbolism, mutilation and ritual.

name: Alexander Payne
signature: Rueful comedies of disappointed Midwestern men.
description: He sets most of his films in ordinary American places, often his native Nebraska, and finds satire and tenderness in small humiliations.

name: Alice Rohrwacher
signature: Rural Italian fables shot on film, between neorealism and fairy tale.
description: Her films treat the disappearing peasant world of central Italy with documentary texture and sudden touches of the miraculous.

name: Andrea Arnold
signature: Sensuous social realism that stays close to young women on the margins.
description: She films housing estates and roadsides in the squarish Academy ratio, with a handheld camera that follows her characters' bodies and attention.

name: Atom Egoyan
signature: Puzzle-like dramas of grief, voyeurism and video.
description: An Armenian-Canadian director whose stories are told out of order, so that the event that hurt everyone comes into focus only gradually.

name: Bi Gan
signature: Dreamlike journeys through Guizhou built around immense single takes.
description: A poet as well as a filmmaker. His films drift between memory and dream and culminate in sequence shots lasting most of an hour.

name: Carlos Reygadas
signature: Sensory, confrontational films made with non-professional casts.
description: A former lawyer who films bodies, weather and landscape with a slow intensity influenced by Tarkovsky and Dreyer.

name: Carlos Saura
signature: Allegories under Franco, then the great dance films of Spain.
description: He evaded censorship with oblique family dramas in which memory and present mingle, and later filmed flamenco and tango as rehearsal and performance.

name: Charlie Kaufman
signature: The screenwriter as auteur: anxious minds turned into nesting-doll narratives.
description: He made his name writing for Spike Jonze and Michel Gondry and then directed his own scripts, in which identity, time and fiction fold into one another.

name: Chloé Zhao
signature: Docu-fictions of the American West, shot at magic hour with people playing themselves.
description: Born in Beijing. She builds scripts around the lives of the non-professionals she casts.

name: Damien Chazelle
signature: Films about the price of ambition, cut and moved like music.
description: A former jazz drummer. His films revive the Hollywood musical and treat performance as an obsessive, physical ordeal.

name: Danny Boyle
signature: Kinetic, music-driven filmmaking across every genre.
description: He came from theatre and television. His films are propelled by pop soundtracks, tilted angles and restless cutting.

name: Darren Aronofsky
signature: Subjective, punishing studies of obsession and the body.
description: His films lock onto a single character's compulsion and push it to collapse, with a camera that follows from just behind the head.

name: Denis Villeneuve
signature: Monumental, slow-burning science fiction and thrillers.
description: A Quebec director who moved from intimate dramas to Hollywood. His films build dread through scale, silence and low, heavy sound.

name: Dušan Makavejev
signature: Anarchic collages of sex and politics from the Yugoslav Black Wave.
description: He intercut fiction, documentary and found footage to mock both Stalinism and Western consumerism.

name: Gaspar Noé
signature: Assaultive, hallucinatory films with a spinning, floating camera.
description: Born in Argentina and based in Paris. He is the best-known director of the French extreme cinema of the 2000s.

name: Greta Gerwig
signature: Fast-talking, warm-hearted films about girls and women becoming themselves.
description: She started as an actress and co-writer in mumblecore films. As a director she rehearses overlapping dialogue with musical precision.

name: Harmony Korine
signature: A provocateur of American trash, from vérité grotesque to neon reverie.
description: He wrote Kids as a teenager and has made deliberately formless, abrasive films about the margins of American life.

name: Jerzy Skolimowski
signature: A restless Polish modernist who made films in exile for decades.
description: A boxer and poet. After a film of his was banned he worked in Britain and elsewhere, returning to Poland late in his career.

name: Joanna Hogg
signature: Quiet, exact studies of the English upper-middle class.
description: She frames her characters at a distance in fixed shots and lets the actors improvise from a prose outline.

name: John Woo
signature: Balletic gunfights and codes of brotherhood.
description: He turned the Hong Kong crime film into operatic spectacle, with two-handed gunplay, slow motion and Christian imagery, and later worked in Hollywood.

name: Kenneth Anger
signature: Occult, homoerotic short films set to pop songs.
description: An underground filmmaker in Los Angeles from his teens. His use of pop songs against ritual imagery shaped music video and directors such as Scorsese and Lynch.

name: Kim Ki-duk
signature: Near-silent parables of cruelty and redemption.
description: A self-taught director who had been a factory worker and painter. His protagonists rarely speak.

name: Kiyoshi Kurosawa
signature: Horror by distance: dread built from empty rooms and wide shots.
description: He came out of low-budget genre films and made Japanese horror into something abstract and existential.

name: László Nemes
signature: A camera fixed to one face while history happens out of focus.
description: His films stay within arm's length of the protagonist in shallow focus, so that atrocity is mostly heard rather than seen.

name: Lav Diaz
signature: Black-and-white epics of Philippine history that last many hours.
description: He treats duration itself as a political act, filming the aftermath of colonialism and dictatorship in very long fixed takes.

name: Luca Guadagnino
signature: Sensual films of desire, appetite and summer light.
description: He lingers on bodies, food, houses and landscapes, and is closely associated with the actress Tilda Swinton.

name: Maren Ade
signature: Comedy of embarrassment allowed to run to its full, painful length.
description: Associated with the Berlin School. Her scenes are heavily rehearsed yet feel discovered in the moment.

name: Miguel Gomes
signature: Playful hybrids of documentary, fable and old-movie romance.
description: A former critic. His films change form halfway through and mix invented stories with real people and places.

name: Mohsen Makhmalbaf
signature: From Islamist militant to the poet of Iranian cinema about cinema.
description: He was jailed under the Shah as a teenager. His films of the 1990s blur re-enactment and reality.

name: Paolo Sorrentino
signature: Baroque, gliding portraits of power, age and Italian excess.
description: A Neapolitan director often seen as Fellini's heir. His films move through parties, palaces and politics with a swooping camera, usually with the actor Toni Servillo.

name: Pawel Pawlikowski
signature: Compressed, black-and-white dramas of postwar Poland.
description: He started in British documentary. His Polish films are framed in the Academy ratio, with characters placed low in the image, and tell decades in under ninety minutes.

name: Peter Greenaway
signature: Films built like paintings and catalogues.
description: Trained as a painter. He organises his films by lists, numbers and alphabets and stages them as tableaux drawn from Dutch and Baroque art.

name: Ryûsuke Hamaguchi
signature: Long conversations in which people slowly say what they could not say.
description: He rehearses by having actors read the script repeatedly without emotion, a method he traces to Renoir.

name: Satoshi Kon
signature: Animated films in which dream, performance and reality cut into each other.
description: He used match cuts and false awakenings to dissolve the line between a character's inner and outer life.

name: Steve McQueen
signature: An artist's unblinking gaze on bodies under extreme pressure.
description: He won the Turner Prize as a video artist before making features. He holds shots long past comfort.

name: Georges Méliès
signature: The stage magician who invented the film trick.
description: He built one of the first film studios and made hundreds of fantasies using stop-motion substitution, multiple exposure and painted sets.

name: Youssef Chahine
signature: The leading figure of Arab cinema, mixing melodrama, musical and politics.
description: Over fifty years in Cairo and Alexandria he moved between popular genres and autobiography.

name: Souleymane Cissé
signature: Mali's great filmmaker, who brought Bambara myth to the screen.
description: He trained in Moscow and made social dramas before turning to the oral traditions of West Africa.

name: Abderrahmane Sissako
signature: Gentle, mosaic-like films about Africa's place in a globalised world.
description: Born in Mauritania, raised in Mali and trained in Moscow. He builds films from loosely connected scenes of daily life.

name: Ken Russell
signature: The flamboyant enfant terrible of British cinema.
description: He made inventive composer biographies for BBC television and then lurid, excessive features about artists, sex and religion.

name: Jean-Pierre Jeunet
signature: Whimsical, sepia-tinted worlds full of contraptions.
description: He began in animation and commercials with Marc Caro. His films are designed down to the last object and shot with distorting wide lenses.

name: Tsui Hark
signature: The producer-director who reinvented the martial-arts film at high speed.
description: Born in Vietnam and trained in Texas. He modernised Hong Kong genre cinema with special effects and frantic editing.

name: Elia Suleiman
signature: Silent comedy of the Palestinian condition.
description: He appears in his own films as a mute observer, in fixed tableaux often compared to Tati and Keaton.

name: Fatih Akin
signature: Raw, music-driven stories from between Germany and Turkey.
description: Born in Hamburg to Turkish parents. His characters move between the two countries in search of love, death and belonging.

name: Mati Diop
signature: Ghost stories of migration between Dakar and Europe.
description: A French-Senegalese director and actress whose films mix documentary and the supernatural.

name: Jirí Menzel
signature: Gentle, ironic comedies of ordinary Czechs under history's weight.
description: The most popular director of the Czechoslovak New Wave, and the regular adapter of the novelist Bohumil Hrabal.

name: Jan Němec
signature: The most radical experimenter of the Czechoslovak New Wave.
description: His allegories of conformity and persecution angered the authorities and he was forced into exile.

name: Lina Wertmüller
signature: Grotesque political comedies of sex and class.
description: She worked as an assistant to Fellini and made a run of loud, argumentative satires in the 1970s with the actor Giancarlo Giannini.

name: Ettore Scola
signature: Bittersweet chronicles of Italian history lived in rooms and at dinner tables.
description: A screenwriter of Italian comedies who became their most reflective director.

name: Ida Lupino
signature: The only woman directing in Hollywood in the 1950s.
description: A star actress who formed her own company to make low-budget films on subjects the studios avoided.

name: Dorothy Arzner
signature: The only woman director of the Hollywood studio era's first decades.
description: She rose from typist to editor to director at Paramount and made films about working women and female friendship.

name: John Frankenheimer
signature: Paranoid thrillers shot with the urgency of live television.
description: He came from live TV drama and brought its deep-focus, wide-angle staging to political thrillers in the 1960s.

name: Robert Siodmak
signature: The German émigré who made some of the darkest film noirs.
description: He began in Berlin, fled the Nazis and at Universal in the 1940s made shadowy thrillers of fate and betrayal.

name: Rouben Mamoulian
signature: A stage innovator who freed the early sound camera.
description: An Armenian-born Broadway director who experimented with moving cameras, layered sound and colour in early talkies.

name: Alan Clarke
signature: British television's fiercest realist, known for relentless walking shots.
description: He made confrontational dramas for the BBC about borstals, skinheads and Northern Ireland, often following characters with a Steadicam.

name: Alanis Obomsawin
signature: The leading documentarian of Indigenous life in Canada.
description: An Abenaki filmmaker who has made dozens of films at the National Film Board about First Nations struggles.

name: Alberto Cavalcanti
signature: A cosmopolitan who linked the French avant-garde, British documentary and Ealing.
description: A Brazilian who worked in Paris, then at the GPO Film Unit and Ealing Studios, where he pushed experiments with sound.

name: Amy Heckerling
signature: Sharp, affectionate comedies of American teenagers.
description: Her high-school films defined teen slang and style for two different decades.

name: Andrew Stanton
signature: A Pixar founder-director with a gift for wordless storytelling.
description: One of the studio's original writers and directors.

name: Angela Schanelec
signature: The most elliptical director of the Berlin School.
description: A former stage actress whose films withhold connections between scenes and show gestures in fragments, in the manner of Bresson.

name: Anthony McCall
signature: Made film into sculpture with a beam of light.
description: A British artist in New York whose 'solid light' works turn the projector beam itself into the artwork.

name: Anthony Minghella
signature: Literate, romantic epics in the David Lean tradition.
description: A playwright turned director of large-scale literary adaptations.

name: Reis & Cordeiro
signature: Poet-ethnographers of Portugal's remote north-east.
description: A poet and a psychiatrist who filmed the villages of Trás-os-Montes as a place where myth and daily life coexist.

name: Anurag Kashyap
signature: The leader of Hindi cinema's gritty independent wave.
description: He broke with Bollywood polish through violent, profane crime stories shot on real streets.

name: Ari Folman
signature: Invented the animated documentary as a memoir of war.
description: An Israeli director who used animation to reconstruct memories that he and fellow soldiers had repressed.

name: Artavazd Peleshian
signature: A poet of montage who made wordless film symphonies.
description: An Armenian filmmaker who devised 'distance montage', in which related images are placed far apart and echo across a film.

name: Arthur Jafa
signature: Collages of found footage that seek a Black visual music.
description: A cinematographer for Julie Dash and Spike Lee who became a major gallery artist.

name: Barbara Hammer
signature: A pioneer of lesbian experimental film.
description: She made around eighty films across five decades, treating the body and hidden queer histories with tactile, layered imagery.

name: Barbara Kopple
signature: Embedded, partisan documentaries of American labour.
description: She lives alongside her subjects for long periods.

name: Baz Luhrmann
signature: Maximalist pop spectacle.
description: An Australian from opera and theatre who mixes periods, styles and anachronistic pop songs at frantic speed.

name: Bette Gordon
signature: A downtown New York director who turned the male gaze around.
description: She came out of the No Wave scene.

name: Bill Douglas
signature: An austere autobiographical trilogy of a Scottish mining childhood.
description: His films compress poverty and neglect into brief, silent, exactly framed scenes.

name: Bill Forsyth
signature: Gentle, off-centre Scottish comedy.
description: He began making films with a Glasgow youth theatre and found humour in small oddities rather than jokes.

name: Bill Gunn
signature: An uncompromising Black modernist of the 1970s.
description: A playwright and actor whose vampire film was really a study of addiction, religion and assimilation.

name: Bill Morrison
signature: Makes films from decaying archival footage.
description: He treats the blisters and rot of old nitrate film as an image of time itself.

name: Billy Woodberry
signature: A key director of the L.A. Rebellion.
description: He was part of the group of Black filmmakers at UCLA who took neorealism as a model.

name: Bo Hu
signature: One four-hour film of despair in a northern Chinese city.
description: A novelist who studied under Béla Tarr in a workshop.

name: Bob Rafelson
signature: A founder of the New Hollywood, as producer and as director of drifters.
description: His films with Jack Nicholson are studies of rootless men.

name: Bruce Baillie
signature: The lyrical West Coast avant-gardist.
description: He made tender, luminous films of the American landscape and its people.

name: Bruce Conner
signature: The father of the found-footage film.
description: An assemblage artist who cut together newsreels, stock footage and countdown leader.

name: Bruce Robinson
signature: One cult comedy of failure, written like literature.
description: An actor and screenwriter.

name: Mayolo & Ospina
signature: The Cali group's satirists of exploitative documentary.
description: Friends from Cali who mixed horror, mock-documentary and politics.

name: Carolee Schneemann
signature: A performance artist who brought the female body into avant-garde film.
description: She painted, scratched and baked the film strip itself.

name: Chick Strand
signature: Sensuous, experimental ethnography.
description: She combined anthropology with a close, moving telephoto camera.

name: Christian Marclay
signature: A sound and video artist who edits film history into new forms.
description: He builds works from thousands of film clips.

name: Chuck Jones
signature: The great stylist of the Warner Bros. cartoon.
description: He directed Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and the Road Runner with expressive poses and rigorous comic logic.

name: Claudia Weill
signature: An early independent portrait of female friendship.
description: She came from documentary.

name: Clio Barnard
signature: Experimental realism from the estates of Bradford.
description: An artist-filmmaker working in the north of England.

name: Curtis Hanson
signature: A classicist craftsman of intelligent genre films.
description: A former film journalist.

name: D.A. Pennebaker
signature: A founder of direct cinema and the concert film.
description: He helped develop portable sync-sound equipment and used it to follow politicians and musicians without narration.

name: Daniels
signature: Maximalist absurdity with a sincere heart.
description: A duo from music videos.

name: David Lowery
signature: Hushed, Malick-influenced American fables.
description: A Texas filmmaker who moves between studio remakes and personal films.

name: David Perlov
signature: A founder of Israeli documentary and of the film diary.
description: Born in Brazil.

name: Zucker, Abrahams & Zucker
signature: The inventors of the modern spoof.
description: A trio from Wisconsin who packed the frame with gags and had serious actors play them straight.

name: Dennis Hopper
signature: The actor whose road movie cracked open Hollywood.
description: A studio actor turned counterculture director.

name: Dino Risi
signature: A master of commedia all'italiana.
description: A former doctor who satirised the Italy of the economic boom.

name: Don Hertzfeldt
signature: Stick figures and existential dread.
description: An independent animator who draws and shoots his films almost alone.

name: Donald Cammell
signature: A painter who made the definitive film of 1960s identity breakdown.
description: He completed only four features.

name: Edgar Morin
signature: The sociologist who, with Jean Rouch, named cinéma vérité.
description: A philosopher who made one landmark film.

name: Edgar Reitz
signature: Chronicler of a German village across the twentieth century.
description: A signatory of the Oberhausen Manifesto.

name: Edgar Wright
signature: Comedy made through editing.
description: He times cuts, whip pans and sound effects to music.

name: Eduardo Coutinho
signature: Brazil's great documentarian of conversation.
description: His later films consist almost entirely of ordinary people talking to him.

name: Euzhan Palcy
signature: A pioneer from Martinique.
description: She filmed the colonial Caribbean from the inside.

name: Farah Khan
signature: A choreographer turned director of knowing Bollywood entertainments.
description: Her films celebrate and parody Hindi film conventions.

name: Florian Henckel von Donnersmarck
signature: A polished classical dramatist of German history.
description: He has made only a few films.

name: Frank Darabont
signature: An old-fashioned storyteller and adapter of Stephen King.
description: A screenwriter turned director.

name: Frantisek Vlácil
signature: A visionary of the medieval world.
description: An art historian who treated film as visual poetry, apart from the Czech New Wave.

name: Garrett Bradley
signature: Lyrical documentaries of Black Southern life.
description: She works between gallery installation and documentary.

name: George Roy Hill
signature: A maker of buddy entertainments.
description: A former pilot and television director.

name: Godfrey Reggio
signature: Wordless films of a world out of balance.
description: A former monk who uses time-lapse and slow motion to contrast nature and technology.

name: Gonzalo García Pelayo
signature: A free spirit of Spain's post-Franco underground.
description: A music producer whose loose films celebrate Andalusia.

name: Grigori Aleksandrov
signature: Eisenstein's collaborator, then the king of the Stalin-era musical.
description: He co-directed with Eisenstein in the 1920s and travelled with him to Hollywood and Mexico.

name: H.C. Potter
signature: A Broadway director remembered for one anarchic comedy.
description: He moved between stage and screen.

name: Hans-Jürgen Syberberg
signature: Stages German history as a Wagnerian puppet theatre of the mind.
description: He works on a sound stage with projections, dolls and monologues to confront German myth.

name: Harun Farocki
signature: The essayist of images as instruments of work, war and control.
description: He made over a hundred films and installations analysing how images are produced and used.

name: Hideaki Anno
signature: Turned the giant-robot genre into a study of depression.
description: Creator of Neon Genesis Evangelion.

name: Hollis Frampton
signature: The theorist-poet of structural film.
description: A photographer and writer whose films are built on systems such as the alphabet.

name: Hugo Santiago
signature: An Argentine modernist close to Borges.
description: A former assistant to Robert Bresson who spent most of his career in France.

name: Humphrey Jennings
signature: The poet of the British home front.
description: A surrealist painter and co-founder of Mass-Observation who made lyrical wartime documentaries.

name: Ildikó Enyedi
signature: Playful, magical Hungarian modernism.
description: She came out of the Béla Balázs experimental studio.

name: Ivan Reitman
signature: Producer-director of the Saturday Night Live generation's blockbusters.
description: A Czechoslovak-born Canadian.

name: Iván Zulueta
signature: A cult film about being devoured by cinema.
description: A poster designer of the Madrid counterculture.

name: Jack Clayton
signature: A fastidious stylist who opened the British New Wave and made a great ghost film.
description: He made few films.

name: Jack Smith
signature: The founder of the camp underground.
description: A New York performance artist.

name: James L. Brooks
signature: A television writer who made talky, humane comedy-dramas.
description: Co-creator of The Mary Tyler Moore Show.

name: Jean Epstein
signature: The theorist of photogénie and a leader of French Impressionist cinema.
description: He explored slow motion and superimposition in the 1920s, then made semi-documentaries in Brittany.

name: Jean Genet
signature: The writer's only film, a silent poem of desire in prison.
description: A novelist and playwright.

name: Jean Grémillon
signature: The underrated master of French cinema of the 1930s and 1940s.
description: A trained musician who brought documentary texture and musical structure to melodrama.

name: Jean-Daniel Pollet
signature: A marginal figure of the New Wave who made a founding essay film.
description: He worked largely alone.

name: Jerry Lewis
signature: The 'total filmmaker' of American comedy.
description: A comedian who wrote, directed and starred in formally inventive comedies revered by French critics.

name: Jiayin Liu
signature: Minimalist films made at home with her parents.
description: She films her own family in their tiny Beijing flat.

name: João Pedro Rodrigues
signature: Portuguese queer cinema as fable and metamorphosis.
description: He trained as a biologist.

name: John Akomfrah
signature: The essayist of the Black British diaspora.
description: A founder of the Black Audio Film Collective.

name: John G. Avildsen
signature: The director of underdog stories.
description: A journeyman who made two of Hollywood's defining underdog films.

name: John Lasseter
signature: The animator who led computer animation into features.
description: A former Disney animator.

name: John McTiernan
signature: The classicist of the modern action film.
description: His action scenes are noted for clear geography and moving-camera staging.

name: John Paizs
signature: A Winnipeg original of deadpan pastiche.
description: Part of the Winnipeg Film Group alongside Guy Maddin.

name: John Sayles
signature: The novelist of American independent film.
description: He writes, directs and edits ensemble dramas about communities and their history.

name: John Smith
signature: Witty British structural film.
description: He plays word against image in films shot around his own London streets.

name: John Sturges
signature: A master of the widescreen ensemble adventure.
description: He specialised in stories of groups of professionals.

name: Joris Ivens
signature: The 'Flying Dutchman' of political documentary.
description: Over six decades he filmed in Spain, China, Vietnam, Cuba and elsewhere, always on the side of the left.

name: Joseph Cornell
signature: The box artist who invented the found-footage film.
description: A reclusive New York artist.

name: Joseph H. Lewis
signature: The stylist of the B movie.
description: He brought bold camera ideas to very low budgets.

name: Juraj Herz
signature: Czechoslovakia's master of the macabre.
description: A Slovak-born puppetry graduate and Holocaust survivor.

name: K. Asif
signature: The maker of Hindi cinema's grandest epic.
description: He completed only two films.

name: Kamal Amrohi
signature: A poet-director of opulent Urdu melodrama.
description: A writer of dialogue and lyrics.

name: Kaneto Shindo
signature: A fiercely independent Japanese director.
description: Born in Hiroshima, he was a screenwriter for Mizoguchi and ran his own production company.

name: Karel Reisz
signature: A founder of Free Cinema and the British New Wave.
description: A Czech-born refugee and critic.

name: Kasi Lemmons
signature: Southern Gothic memory from a Black girl's point of view.
description: An actress turned director.

name: Kathleen Collins
signature: A rediscovered pioneer of Black women's cinema.
description: A writer and professor who died at 46.

name: Katsuhiro Otomo
signature: The manga artist whose film brought anime to the world.
description: He adapted his own manga.

name: Kazuo Hara
signature: Confrontational 'action documentaries'.
description: He follows subjects who provoke society, and provokes them in turn.

name: Kenneth Lonergan
signature: A playwright's cinema of grief and inarticulacy.
description: A New York dramatist.

name: Kidlat Tahimik
signature: The father of Philippine independent cinema.
description: He makes home-made, comic essay films about colonialism.

name: Kinuyo Tanaka
signature: Mizoguchi's great actress, and Japan's second woman director.
description: She directed six features.

name: Kirsten Johnson
signature: A memoir made from a cinematographer's outtakes.
description: A documentary camerawoman for some 25 years.

name: Lasse Hallström
signature: A gentle humanist of childhood.
description: He moved from Sweden to Hollywood literary adaptations.

name: Mulvey & Wollen
signature: Film theory put into practice.
description: Two theorists who made films to test their ideas about a counter-cinema.

name: Len Lye
signature: A pioneer of the film made without a camera.
description: A New Zealand-born artist who painted and scratched directly onto film.

name: Leonardo Favio
signature: A pop singer and Argentina's most poetic director.
description: He moved from Bresson-like austerity to baroque popular myth.

name: Leontine Sagan
signature: Director of a landmark of Weimar and of lesbian cinema.
description: An Austrian-born stage director.

name: Leslie Thornton
signature: An open-ended experimental serial.
description: An avant-garde filmmaker who mixes found and original footage.

name: Lewis Milestone
signature: The director who made the early sound camera move.
description: Born in Russia.

name: Lino Brocka
signature: The conscience of Philippine cinema under Marcos.
description: He fused melodrama and social protest in the slums of Manila.

name: Liu Chia-Liang
signature: The martial artist who made kung fu itself the subject.
description: A real kung fu master and choreographer at Shaw Brothers, also known as Lau Kar-leung.

name: Lizzie Borden
signature: Radical feminist filmmaking on almost no money.
description: She came from the New York art world.

name: Lois Weber
signature: The leading woman director of silent Hollywood.
description: She wrote, produced and directed films on social questions.

name: Lotte Reiniger
signature: The inventor of silhouette animation.
description: She cut her figures from card by hand.

name: Luc Besson
signature: The populist of the French cinéma du look.
description: He turned himself into a one-man studio for international action films.

name: Castaing-Taylor & Paravel
signature: Immersive ethnography from Harvard's Sensory Ethnography Lab.
description: Two anthropologists who replace explanation with overwhelming sensation.

name: Madeline Anderson
signature: A pioneer of Black women's documentary.
description: A television producer and editor.

name: Mani Kaul
signature: The most formally radical director of India's Parallel Cinema.
description: A student of Ritwik Ghatak and admirer of Bresson.

name: Marcel Ophüls
signature: The interrogator of wartime memory.
description: His long interview films set testimonies against each other.

name: Margaret Tait
signature: A film-poet of Orkney.
description: A doctor who made short, self-financed films of people and places close to her.

name: Mariano Llinás
signature: Maximalist storytelling on a tiny budget.
description: A leader of the independent group El Pampero Cine.

name: Marie-Claude Treilhou
signature: Night-shift Paris in three long acts.
description: She came from criticism.

name: Mario Monicelli
signature: A father of commedia all'italiana.
description: His comedies of failure end bitterly.

name: Mario Peixoto
signature: One legendary silent film.
description: He made it at 22 and never completed another.

name: Satrapi & Paronnaud
signature: A graphic memoir of revolutionary Iran, drawn in black and white.
description: Satrapi adapted her own comic with a fellow cartoonist.

name: Mark Robson
signature: An editor who began as a director in Val Lewton's horror unit.
description: He later made large studio melodramas.

name: Mark Sandrich
signature: The director of the best Astaire and Rogers musicals.
description: He let the dances play in long, full-figure takes.

name: Marlen Khutsiev
signature: The voice of the Thaw generation.
description: He filmed young Muscovites drifting through the city and questioning their fathers' legacy.

name: Marlon Riggs
signature: Poetry, performance and polemic on Black gay life.
description: A documentarian and teacher who died of AIDS at 37.

name: Márta Mészáros
signature: Hungary's foremost woman director.
description: Raised partly in the Soviet Union, she makes plain, close-up studies of women's choices.

name: Mathieu Kassovitz
signature: The film that put the French banlieue on screen.
description: An actor and director.

name: Michael Roemer
signature: A neglected American realist.
description: Born in Berlin and sent to England on the Kindertransport.

name: Mira Nair
signature: Vivid portraits of India and its diaspora.
description: She started in documentary.

name: Mohammad-Reza Aslani
signature: A lost Gothic masterpiece of pre-revolutionary Iran.
description: A poet and documentarian.

name: Nelson Pereira dos Santos
signature: The father of Cinema Novo.
description: He brought neorealist methods to Brazil in the 1950s and inspired the younger generation.

name: Nick Park
signature: The clay animator behind Wallace and Gromit.
description: He works in stop-motion at Aardman Animations.

name: Norman McLaren
signature: The great experimenter of the National Film Board of Canada.
description: A Scottish-born animator who drew on film stock, animated live actors and even drew his soundtracks.

name: Norman Z. McLeod
signature: A comedy director who let great clowns do their work.
description: He directed the Marx Brothers and W.C. Fields at Paramount.

name: Oscar Micheaux
signature: The pioneer of African American filmmaking.
description: A former homesteader and novelist who wrote, produced and distributed more than forty 'race films'.

name: Paul King
signature: Warm, meticulously designed family comedy.
description: He came from British television comedy.

name: Paul Vecchiali
signature: An independent who kept faith with 1930s French melodrama.
description: He ran the production company Diagonale and worked very fast on tiny budgets.

name: Philip Kaufman
signature: An intelligent adapter of difficult books.
description: He moves between literary and genre films.

name: Quay Brothers
signature: Stop-motion dreams of dust, dolls and decay.
description: American identical twins based in London, steeped in Central European literature and puppet theatre.

name: Ramesh Sippy
signature: Director of the most famous Hindi film.
description: He works in large-scale popular cinema.

name: Raoul Peck
signature: Haitian political filmmaking.
description: He grew up partly in Congo and served as Haiti's minister of culture.

name: Robert Clouse
signature: The director of Bruce Lee's international breakthrough.
description: A maker of action films.

name: Robert Kramer
signature: A radical American who made political road films from exile in France.
description: A founder of the Newsreel collective.

name: Robert Mulligan
signature: A sensitive director of childhood and memory.
description: He came from live television.

name: Robert Rossen
signature: A hard-edged moralist of ambition and corruption.
description: A screenwriter turned director.

name: Robin Hardy
signature: One film that founded folk horror.
description: He made only three features.

name: Russ Meyer
signature: The cartoonish king of American sexploitation.
description: A former combat cameraman who shot, edited and distributed his own films.

name: Ryan Coogler
signature: Brings personal, political feeling to franchise filmmaking.
description: From Oakland. The actor Michael B. Jordan appears in all his features.

name: Sam Mendes
signature: A stage director with a taste for immaculate images.
description: He works with star cinematographers such as Conrad Hall and Roger Deakins.

name: Sam Raimi
signature: A hyperactive camera and slapstick gore.
description: He began with home-made horror in Michigan and went on to superhero blockbusters.

name: Sam Wood
signature: A reliable MGM craftsman.
description: A studio director from the silent era onward.

name: Samira Makhmalbaf
signature: A prodigy of Iranian cinema.
description: Daughter of Mohsen Makhmalbaf.

name: Sergio Corbucci
signature: The bleakest and most violent of the spaghetti western directors.
description: His westerns are muddy, snowy and politically bitter.

name: Shadi Abdel Salam
signature: One hieratic masterpiece about Egypt's ancient inheritance.
description: A costume and set designer.

name: Shirley Clarke
signature: A dancer who became a leader of the New York independent movement.
description: She blurred staged and documentary film.

name: Steve James
signature: Long-form documentaries of American lives.
description: He follows his subjects over years with Chicago's Kartemquin Films.

name: Stuart Rosenberg
signature: A television veteran with one enduring anti-authority classic.
description: He often worked with Paul Newman.

name: Susan Seidelman
signature: Downtown New York's punk-era comedy.
description: An NYU graduate.

name: Suzan Pitt
signature: Hand-painted psychosexual animation.
description: A painter who animated cel by cel.

name: T. Minh-ha Trinh
signature: A theorist-filmmaker who dismantled the ethnographic film.
description: A Vietnamese-born writer and composer.

name: Ted Kotcheff
signature: A journeyman with one great film about Australia.
description: A Canadian who worked in Britain, Australia and Hollywood.

name: Terry Jones
signature: The Python who directed.
description: A medieval historian as well as a comedian.

name: Tom Tykwer
signature: Kinetic experiments with chance and time.
description: He co-writes his own scores.

name: Tomas Alfredson
signature: Chilly, exact genre films.
description: He came from Swedish television comedy.

name: Toshio Matsumoto
signature: A theorist and pioneer of Japanese experimental film.
description: He mixed documentary, fiction and avant-garde techniques.

name: Ulrike Ottinger
signature: Extravagant costume fantasies and long ethnographic journeys.
description: A painter and photographer.

name: Valie Export
signature: A feminist performance artist who extended her actions into film.
description: An Austrian artist of 'expanded cinema'.

name: Walter Ruttmann
signature: A pioneer of abstract film and of the city symphony.
description: A painter who moved from animated abstraction to rhythmic documentary.

name: Warren Beatty
signature: A star who became a producer, writer and director.
description: He directed only a handful of films.

name: William Dieterle
signature: A German émigré at home in biography and romantic fantasy.
description: He acted for Murnau before emigrating to Hollywood.

name: Yuri Norstein
signature: The poet of cut-out animation.
description: He animates layered paper cut-outs on panes of glass with his wife, the artist Francheska Yarbusova.

name: Zeinabu irene Davis
signature: A later member of the L.A. Rebellion.
description: Her work centres on Black women's history.

name: Zelimir Zilnik
signature: The docu-fiction guerrilla of the Yugoslav Black Wave.
description: He has made low-budget films with marginalised people for over fifty years.

name: Alexander Hammid
signature: A Czech avant-gardist who co-made the most influential American experimental film.
description: Born Alexandr Hackenschmied in Linz, he was a photographer and filmmaker of the Czech avant-garde before emigrating to the United States, where he worked on documentaries and with Maya Deren.

name: Basil Wright
signature: The most lyrical film-maker of the British documentary movement.
description: A member of John Grierson's group at the Empire Marketing Board and the GPO Film Unit, he made poetic documentaries that set images against music and words.

name: Harry Watt
signature: Brought storytelling into British documentary.
description: A GPO Film Unit director who staged real people in scripted scenes, a method he carried into wartime propaganda and then into feature films for Ealing.

name: Hovde & Meyer
signature: The editors who shaped Grey Gardens into a portrait.
description: Ellen Hovde and Muffie Meyer edited and co-directed Grey Gardens with Albert and David Maysles, then made documentaries together for decades.

name: Charlotte Zwerin
signature: The editor-director behind direct cinema's most famous rock film.
description: She edited and co-directed films with the Maysles brothers, including Salesman and Gimme Shelter, and later made portraits of musicians and artists.

name: Clyde Bruckman
signature: Keaton's gag writer and co-director of The General.
description: A former sports reporter who wrote gags for Buster Keaton, Harold Lloyd and Laurel and Hardy, and co-directed some of their best films.

name: Edward Sedgwick
signature: The MGM director of Keaton's last great silent comedies.
description: A studio director of comedies and westerns who directed Buster Keaton's first films at MGM.

name: Donald Crisp
signature: A Griffith actor who co-directed The Navigator.
description: Better known as an actor, he directed silent features in the 1910s and 1920s, including The Navigator with Buster Keaton and Don Q, Son of Zorro with Douglas Fairbanks.

name: Charles Reisner
signature: Directed the cyclone of Steamboat Bill, Jr.
description: A former vaudeville performer who worked with Chaplin and directed comedies for Buster Keaton, Syd Chaplin and later MGM.

name: John G. Blystone
signature: Co-directed Keaton's Our Hospitality.
description: A Fox studio director of comedies and adventure films for two decades.

name: Hamilton Luske
signature: One of the sequence directors behind Disney's classic features.
description: An animator who became a sequence and supervising director on Disney features from Pinocchio to One Hundred and One Dalmatians.

name: Jerome Robbins
signature: The Broadway choreographer who co-directed West Side Story.
description: A leading choreographer of ballet and Broadway, he staged the dances of West Side Story and co-directed the film until he was taken off it during shooting.

name: Ludwig Berger
signature: A Weimar specialist in fairy tale and operetta.
description: A theatre director who made romantic costume films and musicals in Berlin, then worked in Hollywood, the Netherlands and Britain after 1933.

name: Tim Whelan
signature: An American comedy writer who directed in Britain.
description: He wrote gags for Harold Lloyd and directed comedies and thrillers in Britain in the 1930s before co-directing The Thief of Bagdad.

name: Persichetti, Ramsey & Rothman
signature: Made a superhero film look like a comic book in motion.
description: A storyboard artist, an animation director and a comedy writer who co-directed Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse, mixing frame rates, halftone dots and comic panels.

name: Şerif Gören
signature: The director who shot Yol while its author was in prison.
description: A long-time assistant and editor for Yılmaz Güney who became a director in his own right, filming rural and working-class Turkey.

name: Stewart McAllister
signature: Humphrey Jennings's editor.
description: A film editor at the Crown Film Unit whose cutting shaped Jennings's wartime films.

name: William Keighley
signature: A Warner Bros. contract director of gangster films and swashbucklers.
description: A former stage director who made fast, efficient films for Warner Bros. in the 1930s, several with James Cagney.

name: Josh & Benny Safdie
signature: Panic attacks in movie form: New York hustlers filmed in long-lens close-up.
description: Brothers from New York who began with micro-budget films cast partly with people found on the street, then made frantic crime films scored by Oneohtrix Point Never.

name: Ari Aster
signature: Family grief staged as ritual horror.
description: His films begin as domestic or relationship dramas and turn into rites of cult horror, framed with cold symmetry and long, gliding shots.

name: Robert Eggers
signature: Folk horror researched down to the dialect and the candlelight.
description: A former production designer whose films recreate historical worlds with obsessive accuracy, using period language and natural or candle light.

name: Noah Baumbach
signature: Talky, wincing comedies of family and divorce in New York.
description: His films study articulate, self-absorbed New Yorkers through quick, overlapping dialogue, often drawing on his own family life.

name: Spike Jonze
signature: A skate-video and music-video maker who made melancholy fables.
description: He moved from skateboard films and music videos to features that treat loneliness with whimsy, from Charlie Kaufman's puzzles to a love story with an operating system.

name: Todd Solondz
signature: Suburban cruelty played completely straight.
description: His comedies of New Jersey suburbia treat loneliness, abuse and humiliation with a flat, unblinking deadpan.

name: Hal Hartley
signature: Deadpan Long Island romances, spoken like epigrams.
description: His films of the late 1980s and 1990s use flat, aphoristic dialogue, repeated lines and choreographed gestures, with a regular company of actors.

name: Whit Stillman
signature: Comedies of manners about the urban haute bourgeoisie.
description: His films follow articulate, preppy young people talking through love, class and morality, with a dry, Austen-like wit.

name: Gregg Araki
signature: Candy-coloured apocalypses of queer teenage angst.
description: A key figure of the New Queer Cinema whose films mix shoegaze and goth music, saturated colour and nihilistic humour.

name: Larry Clark
signature: A photographer's raw look at teenage lives.
description: His photo books documented drug use among his friends in Tulsa; his films cast real skateboarders and teenagers to show sex and drugs without moralising.

name: Debra Granik
signature: Quiet portraits of Americans living off the grid.
description: She films rural and marginal communities with local non-professionals and an unhurried attention to work and survival.

name: Jeff Nichols
signature: Southern dramas where family love meets dread.
description: From Arkansas, he makes restrained genre films about fathers and families in the American South.

name: Trey Edward Shults
signature: Family trauma filmed with a swirling, music-driven camera.
description: His films treat family conflict as an emergency, with long tracking shots, shifting aspect ratios and loud soundtracks.

name: David Robert Mitchell
signature: Dreamy suburban nightmares of teenage life.
description: His films set coming-of-age stories in timeless Michigan suburbs and in Los Angeles, borrowing the slow dread of John Carpenter.

name: Alex Ross Perry
signature: Abrasive literary comedies about unpleasant people.
description: He shoots on 16mm with tight, handheld close-ups of characters whose wit and cruelty fill every scene.

name: Andrew Bujalski
signature: The godfather of mumblecore.
description: His low-budget comedies of awkward young adults, shot with friends as actors, started the mumblecore wave.

name: Joe Swanberg
signature: The most prolific improviser of mumblecore.
description: He made a long run of cheap, improvised films about relationships, often with fellow filmmakers as actors.

name: Jay & Mark Duplass
signature: Brothers who took mumblecore from festivals to the studios.
description: Their improvised comedies about awkward men and families use restless zooms and handheld camera.

name: Eliza Hittman
signature: Intimate, near-silent films of teenagers on the edges of New York.
description: She films adolescent desire and danger in Brooklyn and on the road with close, grainy images and few words.

name: Josephine Decker
signature: Delirious, sensory films about women's minds.
description: Her films dissolve narrative into texture, with a camera that sways and lunges and soundtracks that unsettle.

name: Kogonada
signature: A video essayist on Ozu who makes films of serene symmetry.
description: He became known for video essays on Ozu, Bresson and Kubrick; his features frame people against modernist architecture.

name: Celine Song
signature: A playwright's quiet romantic what-ifs.
description: A Korean-Canadian playwright whose debut film follows two childhood friends meeting again across decades and continents.

name: Bo Burnham
signature: A YouTube comedian turned chronicler of online life.
description: He grew up performing online; his film and specials examine anxiety and performance in the internet age.

name: Dee Rees
signature: Dramas of Black lives, from Brooklyn to the Mississippi Delta.
description: Her films range from an autobiographical coming-out story to an epic of two families in the postwar Delta.

name: Ava DuVernay
signature: Historical drama and documentary about race and justice in America.
description: A former publicist whose films and series examine the civil rights movement and mass incarceration.

name: Boots Riley
signature: Surreal anti-capitalist satire from an Oakland rapper.
description: Frontman of the hip-hop group The Coup, he turned to film with a surreal comedy about telemarketing and labour.

name: RaMell Ross
signature: Photographic attention to Black lives in the American South.
description: A photographer and teacher in Alabama whose documentary is built from fragments rather than a story; his first fiction feature is shot entirely from its protagonists' points of view.

name: Abel Ferrara
signature: Catholic guilt and New York sleaze.
description: His crime and horror films follow addicts, killers and corrupt cops through New York, searching for grace.

name: Paul Schrader
signature: The critic of transcendental style who wrote Taxi Driver.
description: He wrote or co-wrote Taxi Driver, Raging Bull and The Last Temptation of Christ for Scorsese, and directs films about lonely men keeping diaries, often modelled on Bresson.

name: Walter Hill
signature: Lean, laconic action films.
description: A screenwriter and director of stripped-down westerns and urban action movies with minimal dialogue.

name: Joe Dante
signature: Subversive creature features soaked in cartoon and B-movie lore.
description: A Roger Corman graduate whose monster comedies satirise American suburbia, with cameos from old genre actors.

name: Wes Craven
signature: Reinvented the slasher twice.
description: A former humanities lecturer who made brutal exploitation horror, then the dream-killer Freddy Krueger, then the self-aware Scream.

name: M. Night Shyamalan
signature: Slow-burning suspense and the twist ending.
description: Based in Philadelphia, he makes supernatural thrillers with quiet long takes and endings that reframe what came before.

name: Mike Mills
signature: A graphic designer's essays on parents and memory.
description: A designer and music-video maker whose films about his own father and mother mix narration, photographs and archive images.

name: Panos Cosmatos
signature: Psychedelic, synth-drenched genre reveries.
description: His films soak 1980s genre imagery in red light and slow, heavy synthesiser scores.

name: Alex Garland
signature: A novelist turned director of cerebral science fiction.
description: He wrote The Beach and screenplays for Danny Boyle before directing films about artificial minds, mutation and civil war.

name: Ben Wheatley
signature: Folk horror, hitmen and chaos in the English countryside.
description: He came from viral videos and television comedy; his films mix kitchen-sink realism with occult horror and black comedy.

name: Peter Strickland
signature: Loving pastiches of European cult cinema.
description: His films recreate the textures of 1970s giallo, Eurohorror and erotic cinema with fetishistic attention to sound and objects.

name: Mark Jenkin
signature: Hand-processed black-and-white films of Cornwall.
description: A Cornish director who shoots on clockwork 16mm cameras, develops the film by hand and records all the sound afterwards.

name: Shane Meadows
signature: Funny, violent stories of the English Midlands.
description: He makes semi-autobiographical films about working-class youth in the Midlands with largely untrained casts.

name: Charlotte Wells
signature: A father-daughter holiday reassembled from memory and camcorder tape.
description: A Scottish director whose debut feature recalls a Turkish holiday through the gaps between home video and memory.

name: Lukas Moodysson
signature: Tender, rough films of Swedish teenagers and communes.
description: A poet turned director whose early films about adolescents and a 1970s commune are shot with restless handheld zooms.

name: Nicolas Winding Refn
signature: Neon-lit, near-silent violence.
description: He began with handheld Copenhagen crime films and moved to stylised, slow, colour-saturated thrillers with sparse dialogue.

name: Hlynur Pálmason
signature: Elemental Icelandic dramas of weather and time.
description: His films observe people against the Icelandic landscape, often with time-lapse and long fixed shots.

name: Olivier Assayas
signature: Restless, globetrotting films about art, commerce and ghosts.
description: A former Cahiers du cinéma critic whose fluid camera follows characters through the fashion, film and art worlds, and through recent history.

name: Mia Hansen-Løve
signature: Delicate films of time passing in ordinary lives.
description: A former actress for Olivier Assayas, she makes elliptical films about grief, love and work that cross years in a few cuts.

name: Arnaud Desplechin
signature: Novelistic family sagas from Roubaix.
description: His films are dense, digressive family novels full of quotations, flashbacks and direct address, often with Mathieu Amalric.

name: Bruno Dumont
signature: Mystical films of the French north, from austerity to slapstick.
description: A former philosophy teacher who casts local non-professionals in the Pas-de-Calais, moving from bleak spiritual dramas to grotesque comedy.

name: Alain Guiraudie
signature: Desire and danger in the rural south of France.
description: His films treat sex and longing among working people in Occitanie with frankness, deadpan humour and suspense.

name: François Ozon
signature: A prolific chameleon of French cinema.
description: He makes roughly a film a year, moving between melodrama, musical, thriller and comedy, often with a provocative or queer edge.

name: Philippe Garrel
signature: Black-and-white chronicles of love after May '68.
description: His autobiographical films about lovers, drugs and artistic life in Paris use long takes and few retakes, often with his family as actors.

name: Catherine Breillat
signature: Uncompromising films about female desire.
description: A novelist turned director whose films examine desire, shame and power from young women's points of view.

name: Robin Campillo
signature: Group portraits of activists and outsiders.
description: A screenwriter and editor for Laurent Cantet whose own films capture collective life, most famously the AIDS activists of ACT UP Paris.

name: Alice Diop
signature: A documentarian of France's suburbs and its courts.
description: She made documentaries about the Paris banlieue before a fiction feature built from the transcripts of a real trial.

name: Xavier Dolan
signature: A Quebec prodigy of operatic family melodrama.
description: He directed his first feature at 19 and makes emotionally excessive films about mothers and sons, with pop music and slow motion.

name: Guy Maddin
signature: A Winnipeg fantasist who makes new films that look like lost silent ones.
description: His films imitate the look of decaying early cinema, with iris shots, intertitles and melodrama, to tell feverish stories about family and memory.

name: Christian Petzold
signature: Ghost stories of German history told as melodramas.
description: The best-known director of the Berlin School, he reworks noir and melodrama to show people haunted by the GDR and the Second World War, often with Nina Hoss or Paula Beer.

name: Valeska Grisebach
signature: Westerns of masculinity with non-professional casts.
description: Associated with the Berlin School, she casts non-actors and builds her films slowly from their lives.

name: Ulrich Seidl
signature: Frontal tableaux of Austrian loneliness and cruelty.
description: He stages people in fixed, symmetrical tableaux and blurs documentary and fiction, often provoking audiences with sex and humiliation.

name: Jessica Hausner
signature: Cool, artificial colour and deadpan ambiguity.
description: Her films frame people in stylised colour schemes and fixed shots, leaving miracles and motives unexplained.

name: Lukas Dhont
signature: Tender, wrenching films of adolescent identity.
description: A Belgian director whose films stay close to young protagonists' faces and bodies.

name: Alexander Kluge
signature: The theorist and collagist of the New German Cinema.
description: A lawyer and writer who drafted the Oberhausen Manifesto and made fragmentary essay films mixing fiction, documents and commentary.

name: Margarethe von Trotta
signature: Political history told through women's lives.
description: An actress turned director, she makes films about sisters, terrorists and intellectuals, often with Barbara Sukowa.

name: Aleksei Balabanov
signature: The poet of 1990s Russian chaos.
description: His gangster films became cult classics of post-Soviet Russia, while his other films are bleak period pieces about cruelty.

name: Kantemir Balagov
signature: Harrowing postwar dramas in green and red.
description: A student of Aleksandr Sokurov whose films about women after trauma are built on saturated colour and long close shots.

name: Sergei Loznitsa
signature: Archival and observational films of mass history.
description: Raised in Kyiv, he alternates found-footage documentaries about Soviet and Nazi history with bleak fictions.

name: Kirill Serebrennikov
signature: Theatrical bravura about artists and dissidents.
description: A stage director whose films fold music, fantasy and long takes into stories of Soviet rock, illness and exile.

name: Radu Jude
signature: Rude, essayistic satire of Romanian history.
description: He moved from realist dramas to collage and essay films that confront Romania's history of slavery and its part in the Holocaust.

name: Corneliu Porumboiu
signature: Deadpan comedies about language and meaning.
description: His films turn arguments over words, definitions and evidence into dry comedy.

name: Agnieszka Holland
signature: A Polish director of moral anxiety and modern history.
description: She worked with Andrzej Wajda in Poland's cinema of moral anxiety, then made films abroad about the Holocaust, totalitarianism and Europe's borders.

name: Krzysztof Zanussi
signature: A physicist's cinema of moral and intellectual dilemmas.
description: Trained in physics and philosophy, he made cerebral dramas central to Poland's cinema of moral anxiety.

name: Otar Iosseliani
signature: Wry, wandering comedies of idlers, from Tbilisi to Paris.
description: A Georgian musician turned filmmaker whose gentle, nearly wordless comedies drift between many characters.

name: Tengiz Abuladze
signature: Made the allegory that broke the Soviet silence about the terror.
description: His trilogy of Georgian parables ended with Repentance, a grotesque satire of a Stalin-like dictator released during glasnost.

name: Athina Rachel Tsangari
signature: A founder of the Greek Weird Wave.
description: A producer of the movement's early films whose own work stages strange, awkward behaviour with deadpan humour.

name: Albert Serra
signature: Languid, decadent tableaux of historical figures.
description: A Catalan provocateur whose films about Don Quixote, the Magi, Casanova and Louis XIV are made of long, improvised takes.

name: Mario Bava
signature: The father of Italian Gothic horror and the giallo.
description: A former cinematographer who painted his horror films in saturated colour and shadow on tiny budgets.

name: Matteo Garrone
signature: Fairy tales and crime stories from Italy's margins.
description: A former painter whose films range from the Camorra epic Gomorrah to fables and folk tales.

name: Lisandro Alonso
signature: Wordless journeys of solitary men through remote landscapes.
description: His films follow non-professional loners working and wandering in jungle, forest and pampas, in very long takes.

name: Matías Piñeiro
signature: Playful variations on Shakespeare among young Argentine women.
description: His films, mostly set among young actresses rehearsing and gossiping in Buenos Aires, riff on Shakespeare's comedies.

name: Kleber Mendonça Filho
signature: A critic's portraits of Recife, between social drama and genre film.
description: A former critic whose films about the city of Recife study class, property and memory, sometimes erupting into violence.

name: Pablo Larraín
signature: Dark portraits of Chile under Pinochet, and of icons in crisis.
description: His films about the Pinochet era are grim and absurd; later he made portraits of famous women at breaking point.

name: Ciro Guerra
signature: Indigenous Colombia filmed as myth.
description: His films about Amazonian and Wayuu communities, several co-directed with Cristina Gallego, mix ethnography with epic.

name: Amat Escalante
signature: Shocking, deadpan violence in contemporary Mexico.
description: He films brutal stories of poverty and cartel violence in fixed, patient shots.

name: Diao Yinan
signature: Chinese film noir in neon and snow.
description: A playwright turned director whose crime films set noir plots in the grubby underworld of provincial Chinese cities.

name: Lou Ye
signature: Passionate, handheld films of desire, banned more than once.
description: His sensual, fragmentary love stories have repeatedly run into Chinese censorship.

name: Johnnie To
signature: Hong Kong's master of geometric gunfights and gangster ritual.
description: Through his company Milkyway Image he made precisely choreographed crime films about loyalty and fate.

name: Ann Hui
signature: A humane chronicler of Hong Kong and its people.
description: A leading figure of the Hong Kong New Wave of 1979, she has made social dramas, literary adaptations and stories of migrants and the elderly for four decades.

name: Stanley Kwan
signature: Melancholy melodramas of memory and desire.
description: A former assistant to Ann Hui, he made elegant films about women and about queer Hong Kong.

name: Na Hong-jin
signature: Relentless Korean thrillers that turn into horror.
description: His films start as police or chase thrillers and end in exhausting, ambiguous violence and the supernatural.

name: Kim Jee-woon
signature: A stylist who has made a film in almost every genre.
description: His films move between horror, gangster film, western and spy thriller, each staged with polish and dark humour.

name: Naomi Kawase
signature: Lyrical films of Nara's forests, family and death.
description: She began with diary documentaries about her own family and makes fiction films with the same intimate, nature-filled camera.

name: Takashi Miike
signature: Japan's most prolific and outrageous genre director.
description: He has made more than a hundred films, from direct-to-video yakuza films to period epics, notorious for extreme violence and absurdity.

name: Sion Sono
signature: Excessive, anarchic films of faith and family.
description: A poet turned director whose long, wild films mix religion, voyeurism, violence and melodrama.

name: Shunji Iwai
signature: Bittersweet youth films in soft, overexposed light.
description: A music-video director whose films about adolescence and memory use bleached colour and a drifting handheld camera.

name: Shinji Sōmai
signature: A master of the extremely long take.
description: His films about teenagers and families are built from long, often single-shot scenes that push his young actors hard.

name: Nobuhiko Obayashi
signature: Psychedelic, handmade fantasies from a former commercials director.
description: He made experimental shorts and television commercials before his debut House, and late in life a series of collage-like anti-war films.

name: Mamoru Oshii
signature: Philosophical anime of cities, dogs and machines.
description: His animated films slow down for long, contemplative city sequences and debates about identity and reality.

name: Masaaki Yuasa
signature: Rubbery, hallucinatory animation.
description: His films and series stretch bodies and perspective with free, sketchy drawing and a manic pace.

name: Makoto Shinkai
signature: Photo-real skies and long-distance love.
description: He began by animating a short almost entirely alone on his computer; his features are melancholy romances under luminous skies.

name: Mamoru Hosoda
signature: Family adventures across real and virtual worlds.
description: His animated films alternate between digital worlds and rural Japan to tell stories of families and growing up.

name: Mani Ratnam
signature: Tamil cinema's great stylist of romance and politics.
description: His films set love stories against riots, terrorism and war, with songs by A. R. Rahman and lush camera work.

name: Mrinal Sen
signature: The political modernist of Bengali cinema.
description: Alongside Satyajit Ray and Ritwik Ghatak, he made Bengali cinema's most overtly political and formally playful films.

name: Shyam Benegal
signature: The founder of Hindi parallel cinema's realist strand.
description: A former advertising filmmaker whose rural dramas of caste and exploitation launched a generation of actors.

name: Adoor Gopalakrishnan
signature: Kerala's master of quiet, precise films about decline.
description: A pioneer of Malayalam art cinema whose films study feudal decline and inner life with restraint.

name: Payal Kapadia
signature: Dreamlike films of women in Mumbai.
description: Her films blend documentary and fiction, letters and night-time city scenes.

name: Chaitanya Tamhane
signature: Patient, observational dramas of Mumbai's institutions.
description: He films courtrooms and music lessons in long, static wide shots, letting the system reveal itself.

name: Majid Majidi
signature: Tender films of children and faith.
description: His simple, emotional stories about poor children and families found audiences around the world.

name: Mohammad Rasoulof
signature: Dissident parables of complicity under the Islamic Republic.
description: Repeatedly banned from filmmaking, he makes films clandestinely about ordinary people forced into moral compromise.

name: Nadine Labaki
signature: Lebanese ensemble comedies and street-level melodramas.
description: An actress-director whose films cast non-professionals to tell stories of Beirut's women and children.

name: Kaouther Ben Hania
signature: Hybrids of documentary and re-enactment from Tunisia.
description: Her films question how stories are told, staging real people alongside actors.

name: Mahamat-Saleh Haroun
signature: Austere fables of fathers and sons in Chad.
description: The leading director of Chad, he makes spare dramas about war, revenge and family.

name: Alain Gomis
signature: Music-filled portraits of African cities.
description: A French-Senegalese director whose films follow characters through Dakar and Kinshasa, with music at their centre.

name: Haile Gerima
signature: The L.A. Rebellion's fiercest political voice.
description: An Ethiopian-born director who studied at UCLA and made radical films about Black life in Los Angeles, about slavery and about Ethiopia.

name: Rithy Panh
signature: Documents the Khmer Rouge genocide that he survived.
description: A survivor of the Khmer Rouge labour camps, he makes documentaries that confront perpetrators and reconstruct memory.

name: Brillante Mendoza
signature: Street-level realism of Manila.
description: He films poverty, crime and survival in the Philippines in a raw, handheld style.

name: Taika Waititi
signature: Deadpan whimsy from New Zealand.
description: He moved from small comedies about awkward children and vampire flatmates to superhero blockbusters.

name: Warwick Thornton
signature: Aboriginal stories from Central Australia, shot by the director himself.
description: A cinematographer and director from Alice Springs who films Aboriginal lives with few words and vast landscapes.

name: Alice Guy-Blaché
signature: The first woman director, and one of the first to tell stories on film.
description: Secretary to Léon Gaumont, she began directing narrative films for his company in 1896, ran its production for a decade, then founded her own studio, Solax, in the United States.

name: Edwin S. Porter
signature: Edison's director, who built The Great Train Robbery from separate shots.
description: A projectionist who became Thomas Edison's leading film-maker, he assembled stories from shots taken in different places and times, an early basis of film editing.

name: Max Linder
signature: The dapper star of early French film comedy, a model for Chaplin.
description: Pathé's biggest star before the First World War, he wrote and directed comedies about his elegant, unlucky man-about-town, and later made features in Hollywood.

name: Mack Sennett
signature: The 'King of Comedy' whose Keystone studio made slapstick an industry.
description: A former Griffith actor who founded Keystone in 1912, producing and often directing chaotic chase comedies with the Keystone Cops and giving Chaplin his start in film.

name: Thomas H. Ince
signature: The producer who organised film-making around the shooting script.
description: A director turned producer who built Inceville, a studio ranch near Santa Monica, and ran production from detailed continuity scripts, a model for the Hollywood studio system.

name: Allan Dwan
signature: A director of some 400 films, from the earliest Westerns to 1950s Technicolor.
description: An engineer who drifted into films in 1909, he directed Douglas Fairbanks's Robin Hood and Gloria Swanson's comedies, then Shirley Temple films and lean, colourful B-films.

name: Rex Ingram
signature: The painterly director who made Valentino a star.
description: An Irish-born sculptor turned director whose lavish, pictorial epics of the early 1920s were among the biggest hits of the silent era; he later ran his own studio in Nice.

name: Germaine Dulac
signature: A pioneer of French impressionist and surrealist film, and a feminist critic.
description: A journalist and feminist who became a leading figure of the French avant-garde in the 1920s, writing about 'pure cinema' and making films that render a character's inner life in images.

name: Marcel L'Herbier
signature: The aesthete of French impressionism, who built films like modernist exhibitions.
