description: A poet and dramatist who made stylised films with leading architects and painters, and later founded IDHEC, the French national film school.

name: Jacques Feyder
signature: The Belgian director of Carnival in Flanders and teacher of Marcel Carné.
description: Working in France, Hollywood and Britain, he made polished literary adaptations and satires, and his realism shaped the poetic realist films of his assistant Marcel Carné.

name: Paul Leni
signature: A set designer whose expressionist style carried into Hollywood horror.
description: A painter and set designer who directed the expressionist anthology Waxworks, then moved to Universal, where his shadowy, angular style shaped the studio's horror films.

name: Paul Wegener
signature: The actor-director who brought the Golem to the screen.
description: A leading actor of Max Reinhardt's company who saw film as a medium for the fantastic, he co-directed and starred in The Student of Prague and three films about the Golem of Jewish legend.

name: E. A. Dupont
signature: Directed Variety, whose swinging camera dazzled Hollywood.
description: A film critic turned director whose circus melodrama Variety, shot by Karl Freund with a camera that flies with the trapeze artists, led to work in Britain and Hollywood.

name: Arnold Fanck
signature: Inventor of the German mountain film.
description: A geologist who filmed skiers and climbers on real peaks and built melodramas around the danger of the Alps; Leni Riefenstahl started as his actress.

name: Hans Richter
signature: A Dada artist who made some of the first abstract films.
description: A painter of the Dada movement who animated geometric shapes in his Rhythmus films of the early 1920s, then taught in New York and made Dreams That Money Can Buy with Duchamp, Ernst, Léger and Man Ray.

name: Mauritz Stiller
signature: The Swedish director who discovered Greta Garbo.
description: With Victor Sjöström he led the golden age of Swedish silent film, moving between sophisticated comedies and literary sagas, and took Garbo with him to Hollywood.

name: Benjamin Christensen
signature: Director of Häxan, a silent essay film on witchcraft.
description: A Danish actor and director whose Häxan mixes lecture, engravings and staged scenes of devils and witches, before he worked in Hollywood on horror films.

name: Yakov Protazanov
signature: The most popular film-maker of tsarist Russia, who returned to make Aelita.
description: He directed literary adaptations before the revolution, emigrated, then came back in 1923 to make the science-fiction film Aelita, with constructivist sets, followed by popular comedies.

name: Lev Kuleshov
signature: The teacher whose experiments gave montage its first theory.
description: At the state film school he ran a workshop that tested how editing creates meaning, the 'Kuleshov effect', and taught Pudovkin and Barnet, while directing satires and a Western.

name: Vsevolod Pudovkin
signature: The montage director who told the revolution through a mother's awakening.
description: A chemist turned film-maker trained by Kuleshov, he linked shots into an emotional chain and told history through individual characters, and wrote influential books on film technique.

name: Grigori Kozintsev
signature: Co-founder of the Factory of the Eccentric Actor, later the director of a great Soviet Hamlet.
description: With Leonid Trauberg he founded FEKS in Petrograd in 1921 and made grotesque, eccentric silents and the Maxim trilogy, then alone filmed Shakespeare with music by Shostakovich.

name: Abram Room
signature: Director of Bed and Sofa, a frank silent comedy of a Moscow ménage à trois.
description: A doctor turned director whose intimate films about everyday Soviet life, shot partly on the streets of Moscow, stood apart from the epics of montage.

name: Esfir Shub
signature: Invented the compilation film from old newsreels.
description: An editor who recut imported films for Soviet audiences, she assembled The Fall of the Romanov Dynasty from tsarist newsreels and home movies, founding the archive documentary.

name: John Grierson
signature: Founder of the British documentary movement, who gave 'documentary' its meaning.
description: A Scottish producer who set up film units at the Empire Marketing Board, the GPO and the National Film Board of Canada, directing only Drifters himself and training a generation of film-makers.

name: Winsor McCay
signature: The comic-strip artist who made animation an art.
description: Creator of the strip Little Nemo in Slumberland, he drew thousands of frames by hand for Gertie the Dinosaur and The Sinking of the Lusitania, giving characters weight and personality.

name: Ladislas Starevich
signature: Pioneer of stop-motion puppet film, starting with real insects.
description: An entomologist who animated preserved beetles in Russia, then in France made intricate puppet films, including the feature The Tale of the Fox.

name: Fleischer Brothers
signature: The New York rivals of Disney, behind Betty Boop and Popeye.
description: Max invented the rotoscope and ran the studio, Dave directed: their surreal, jazz-scored cartoons of Koko the Clown, Betty Boop and Popeye were looser and stranger than Disney's.

name: Tex Avery
signature: The cartoon director of speed, wild takes and broken rules.
description: At Warner Bros. he shaped Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, and at MGM made frantic cartoons that stretch bodies to extremes and talk to the audience across the frame.

name: Oskar Fischinger
signature: The master of abstract animation set to music.
description: In Berlin he animated wax, paper and paint into visual music, then in Hollywood worked briefly on Disney's Fantasia, whose abstract opening draws on his ideas.

name: Jiří Trnka
signature: The master of the puppet film, called the 'Walt Disney of the East'.
description: A painter and illustrator who made Czech stop-motion puppet features into a national art, from folk tales to A Midsummer Night's Dream, with fixed faces that light alone makes expressive.

name: Karel Zeman
signature: Brought Jules Verne's engravings to life.
description: He combined live actors with animation, puppets and painted backdrops styled like 19th-century engravings, making fantastic voyages after Jules Verne and Baron Munchausen.

name: Jan Švankmajer
signature: The Czech surrealist of stop-motion, food, flesh and childhood fears.
description: A member of the Czech surrealist group who animates objects, meat and clay in tactile, grotesque close-ups, from Dimensions of Dialogue to his feature version of Alice.

name: Brad Bird
signature: The Pixar director who brought the action film into animation.
description: Trained by Disney veterans, he directed The Iron Giant at Warner Bros., then The Incredibles and Ratatouille at Pixar, before moving to live action.

name: Harry Smith
signature: Folklorist, occultist and maker of hand-painted abstract films.
description: The compiler of the Anthology of American Folk Music also painted directly on film and made Heaven and Earth Magic, a cut-out animation of Victorian engravings.

name: Peter Kubelka
signature: Builds 'metric films' frame by frame.
description: An Austrian film-maker who composes very short films from single frames, as in Arnulf Rainer, and co-founded the Austrian Film Museum and Anthology Film Archives in New York.

name: Ken Jacobs
signature: Pulled a 1905 short apart, frame by frame, in Tom, Tom, the Piper's Son.
description: A New York artist who reworks found footage to study perception, re-filming early cinema in close detail and later creating 3D effects in his Nervous System performances.

name: James Benning
signature: Films American landscapes in long, fixed shots.
description: A former mathematics teacher who records rural and industrial America in long static takes, letting light, sound and passing traffic become the subject.

name: Su Friedrich
signature: Personal essay films about family, faith and lesbian identity.
description: An American experimental film-maker who works with text on screen, found footage and her own family history, as in Sink or Swim, about her father, told in 26 sections, one for each letter of the alphabet.

name: Marco Bellocchio
signature: Italian cinema's lifelong rebel against family, church and state.
description: His debut Fists in the Pocket, about an epileptic young man who sets out to kill his family, made him a figure of 1960s revolt; later films revisit Italian history, from Mussolini to the Moro kidnapping.

name: Liliana Cavani
signature: Director of The Night Porter, and of Francis of Assisi three times over.
description: She began with historical documentaries for Italian television, then made provocative films about power, faith and sexuality, returning to Francis of Assisi across five decades.

name: Valerio Zurlini
signature: A melancholic stylist of doomed love and waiting.
description: A director of restrained, elegiac films, from Family Diary with Marcello Mastroianni to The Desert of the Tartars, about soldiers waiting for an enemy who never comes.

name: Luigi Comencini
signature: The commedia all'italiana director most attuned to children.
description: He moved from neorealist-tinged comedies such as Bread, Love and Dreams to social satire, and returned often to childhood, from Misunderstood to a celebrated television Pinocchio.

name: Vittorio De Seta
signature: Filmed the vanishing work of Sicilian and Sardinian peasants and fishermen.
description: His short documentaries of the 1950s, in colour and widescreen and without commentary, record tuna fishing, sulphur mining and harvests in the south; his feature Bandits of Orgosolo was cast with Sardinian shepherds.

name: Alberto Lattuada
signature: An eclectic stylist who co-directed Fellini's first film.
description: A cultured, versatile director of literary adaptations and neorealist dramas, he co-directed Variety Lights with Federico Fellini and later made sensual comedies.

name: Julien Duvivier
signature: The craftsman of poetic realism behind Pépé le Moko.
description: A prolific director of fatalistic dramas in the 1930s, notably Pépé le Moko with Jean Gabin in the Casbah of Algiers, who worked in Hollywood during the war and later made the Don Camillo comedies.

name: Sacha Guitry
signature: The playwright who narrated his films and played everyone's favourite cad.
description: The most celebrated French dramatist of his day turned his wit to film, inventing playful narrated forms, as in The Story of a Cheat, told in his own voice over the images.

name: Claude Sautet
signature: Chronicler of French middle-class friendships and love.
description: He made ensemble films around cafés and dinners with Yves Montand, Romy Schneider and Michel Piccoli, then late films of great restraint, Un cœur en hiver and Nelly and Monsieur Arnaud.

name: Bertrand Tavernier
signature: A cinephile director and historian across genres, from crime to jazz.
description: A critic and press agent turned director, he made period films, crime dramas and Round Midnight, about an American jazz musician in Paris, and wrote widely on American cinema.

name: André Téchiné
signature: A lyrical director of desire and youth in the French southwest.
description: A former Cahiers critic whose films move between eras and lovers with restless camerawork, as in Wild Reeds, about boarding-school friends during the Algerian war.

name: Pierre Étaix
signature: Tati's collaborator who revived silent burlesque in the 1960s.
description: A clown and gag writer who worked on Mon Oncle, then directed his own melancholy comedies full of sound gags; they were long unseen because of a rights dispute until their restoration in 2010.

name: Jacques Rozier
signature: The free-spirited outsider of the New Wave, of holidays by the sea.
description: His Adieu Philippine, about a young man awaiting military service in Algeria who flirts with two girls on holiday in Corsica, captured the New Wave's spontaneity; he made few, loose, improvised films after it.

name: Bertrand Blier
signature: Provocative, absurd comedies of male desire.
description: The son of the actor Bernard Blier, he made Going Places with Gérard Depardieu and Patrick Dewaere, then increasingly surreal farces about couples and conventions.

name: Jean-Jacques Beineix
signature: Launched the glossy 'cinéma du look' with Diva.
description: His Diva, a thriller about an opera fan and a bootleg recording, defined a stylish French cinema of colour and surface in the 1980s, followed by the passionate Betty Blue.

name: Konrad Wolf
signature: The leading director of East German cinema.
description: Raised in exile in Moscow, he returned with the Red Army in 1945, as he recounts in I Was Nineteen, and became DEFA's most respected director and president of the East German Academy of Arts.

name: Frank Beyer
signature: DEFA director of Jacob the Liar and the banned Trace of Stones.
description: His Trace of Stones, about a defiant construction foreman, was withdrawn days after its release in 1966; later Jacob the Liar became the only East German film nominated for an Oscar.

name: Wolfgang Staudte
signature: Made the first German feature after the war, among the ruins of Berlin.
description: His The Murderers Are Among Us, shot in bombed Berlin for the new DEFA studio, confronts a doctor's guilt; he worked in both German states and satirised obedience to authority in The Kaiser's Lackey.

name: Helmut Käutner
signature: A poetic stylist who kept his distance from Nazi propaganda while working inside the industry.
description: A cabaret writer turned director whose wartime films, such as Romance in a Minor Key and Under the Bridges, tell quiet, lyrical stories, and who later made The Devil's General.

name: Werner Schroeter
signature: The operatic extremist of New German Cinema.
description: Devoted to opera and to Maria Callas, he made stylised, ecstatic films of grand emotion, admired by Fassbinder, from Eika Katappa to The Kingdom of Naples.

name: Rosa von Praunheim
signature: His 1971 film launched the West German gay rights movement.
description: A provocateur of queer cinema whose It Is Not the Homosexual Who Is Perverse, But the Society in Which He Lives sparked activist groups after its screenings, followed by decades of documentaries and camp melodramas.

name: Helma Sanders-Brahms
signature: Told the war through her mother's eyes in Germany, Pale Mother.
description: A leading woman director of New German Cinema whose Germany, Pale Mother follows a mother and daughter through the bombing and the hungry postwar years, narrated by the director herself.

name: Tony Richardson
signature: Brought the Angry Young Men from the stage to the screen.
description: A founder of Free Cinema who directed Look Back in Anger on stage and screen, he shot northern working-class life on location, then won Oscars with the bawdy period romp Tom Jones.

name: Anthony Asquith
signature: The prime minister's son who filmed Shaw, Wilde and Rattigan.
description: Son of H. H. Asquith, he made the expressive silent Underground, then polished adaptations of Shaw, Wilde and Terence Rattigan, including Pygmalion and The Importance of Being Earnest.

name: Thorold Dickinson
signature: A precise stylist of British gothic, and of the first British film-studies department.
description: His Gaslight was suppressed by MGM to make way for its own remake, and The Queen of Spades became a cult film; he later founded the first university film department in Britain, at the Slade.

name: Basil Dearden
signature: Ealing's maker of social-problem thrillers.
description: With the producer Michael Relph he made polished dramas and thrillers about race, crime and homosexuality, notably Victim, the first English-language film to use the word 'homosexual'.

name: Charles Crichton
signature: Ealing comedy director who returned decades later for A Fish Called Wanda.
description: An editor turned director of Ealing comedies, including The Lavender Hill Mob and The Titfield Thunderbolt, who after years in television co-wrote and directed A Fish Called Wanda with John Cleese.

name: Juan Antonio Bardem
signature: A communist director who criticised Franco's Spain from inside it.
description: With Luis García Berlanga he set out to renew Spanish cinema, making Death of a Cyclist and Main Street, stories of guilt and provincial hypocrisy; he was arrested during the shooting of the latter.

name: José Luis Guerín
signature: A Catalan film-maker of looking, between documentary and fiction.
description: He makes quiet films that blur documentary and fiction, from Construction Site, about a building going up in Barcelona's Raval, to In the City of Sylvia, about a young man following a woman through Strasbourg.

name: João César Monteiro
signature: Portuguese cinema's scandalous poet, playing his own lecherous alter ego.
description: A critic and poet who cast himself as João de Deus, a gaunt, erudite libertine, in a trilogy of comic films of desire and literature, and ended with an almost black screen in Snow White.

name: Paulo Rocha
signature: Opened the new Portuguese cinema with The Green Years.
description: After assisting Jean Renoir and Manoel de Oliveira, he made The Green Years, about a young shoemaker from the country lost in Lisbon, and later films drawn to Japan.

name: Michael Cacoyannis
signature: Director of Zorba the Greek and of filmed Greek tragedy.
description: A Cypriot-born director who made Stella with Melina Mercouri, adapted Euripides with Irene Papas, and had his greatest success with Zorba the Greek.

name: Metin Erksan
signature: His Dry Summer won the Golden Bear for Turkey.
description: A central figure of Turkish cinema's golden age, he made Dry Summer, about a farmer who dams a stream to deny water to his neighbours, and Time to Love, a mystical romance.

name: Ömer Kavur
signature: A Turkish modernist of solitude and obsession.
description: Trained in Paris, he made introspective films of loneliness and enigmatic journeys, such as Motherland Hotel, about a provincial hotel clerk, and The Secret Face.

name: Susanne Bier
signature: Danish director of family melodramas, from Dogme to international drama.
description: She made Open Hearts under the Dogme rules, then glossier international dramas and the television series The Night Manager.

name: Cai Chusheng
signature: The left-wing melodramatist of Shanghai cinema, and co-director of The Spring River Flows East.
description: A leading director at the Lianhua studio in the 1930s, he made melodramas about fishermen, workers and modern women, and after the war co-directed the two-part family epic The Spring River Flows East with Zheng Junli.

name: Sun Yu
signature: Lianhua's 'poet director', whose silent films joined romance to social and patriotic causes.
description: Trained in the United States, he returned to Shanghai and made lyrical films at Lianhua about workers, peasants and young women, several ending in calls to resist Japan.

name: Wu Yonggang
signature: Directed The Goddess, the best-known film of China's silent era.
description: A set designer who turned director at Lianhua, he made The Goddess, about a woman who sells herself to pay for her son's schooling, with Ruan Lingyu in the lead.

name: Yuan Muzhi
signature: His Street Angel mixes songs, slapstick and tragedy in the alleys of 1930s Shanghai.
description: An actor and critic who directed two films: Scenes of City Life, a satirical musical, and Street Angel, with Zhou Xuan and Zhao Dan as poor lovers in a Shanghai tenement. After 1949 he led the new state's film bureau.

name: Frank Lloyd
signature: Won two directing Oscars and made the 1935 Mutiny on the Bounty.
description: A Scottish-born actor who became one of Hollywood's most prolific directors from the silent era on, known for large historical dramas.

name: Norman Taurog
signature: Held the record as the youngest winner of the directing Oscar, for Skippy, until 2017.
description: A studio director of comedies, musicals and child-star vehicles from the 1920s to the late 1960s, from Skippy and Boys Town to nine films with Elvis Presley.

name: Franklin J. Schaffner
signature: Directed Patton and the original Planet of the Apes.
description: Came from live television drama of the 1950s and made large-scale films in the late 1960s and 1970s, from Planet of the Apes to Patton and Papillon.

name: Robert Benton
signature: Co-wrote Bonnie and Clyde, then directed Kramer vs. Kramer.
description: An art director at Esquire who co-wrote Bonnie and Clyde with David Newman, then directed quiet, actor-centred dramas such as Kramer vs. Kramer and Places in the Heart.

name: Robert Redford
signature: The star who won a directing Oscar with his first film and founded Sundance.
description: One of the biggest film stars of the 1970s, he directed restrained family and moral dramas from Ordinary People on, and founded the Sundance Institute in 1981.

name: Richard Attenborough
signature: Directed Gandhi, with one of the largest crowd scenes ever filmed.
description: An English actor who turned director with Oh! What a Lovely War and spent two decades bringing Gandhi to the screen, followed by films about Steve Biko and Chaplin.

name: Barry Levinson
signature: Made four films set in his home town, Baltimore, starting with Diner.
description: A comedy writer who began directing with Diner, a talk-filled portrait of young men in 1959 Baltimore, and went on to Rain Man and Wag the Dog.

name: Kevin Costner
signature: Won Best Director with his first film, the Western Dances with Wolves.
description: A leading man of the late 1980s and 1990s who directed long, unhurried Westerns, from Dances with Wolves to the Horizon saga.

name: Mel Gibson
signature: Directed Braveheart and films spoken in Aramaic and Yucatec Maya.
description: An Australian-raised star of Mad Max and Lethal Weapon whose films as director dwell on physical suffering and sacrifice, from Braveheart to The Passion of the Christ and Apocalypto.

name: Ron Howard
signature: The child actor of The Andy Griffith Show who directed Apollo 13 and A Beautiful Mind.
description: Grew up on television as Opie Taylor and Richie Cunningham, then became a reliable director of mainstream dramas and comedies, from Splash to Apollo 13 and Rush.

name: Tom Hooper
signature: Directed The King's Speech, framed with wide lenses against bare walls.
description: Came from British television and made polished period dramas, with off-centre wide-angle framing in The King's Speech and singing recorded live on set for Les Misérables.

name: Michel Hazanavicius
signature: Made The Artist, a black-and-white silent film that won Best Picture.
description: A French director of pastiches, from the OSS 117 spy spoofs to The Artist, a silent black-and-white comedy about Hollywood's move to sound.

name: William A. Wellman
signature: Directed Wings, winner of the first Best Picture.
description: A First World War pilot who directed hard-edged studio films across genres, from Wings and The Public Enemy to The Ox-Bow Incident.

name: Harry Beaumont
signature: Directed The Broadway Melody, the first sound film to win Best Picture.
description: A prolific silent-era director at MGM whose backstage musical The Broadway Melody helped set the pattern for the Hollywood musical.

name: Wesley Ruggles
signature: Directed Cimarron, the land-rush Western that won Best Picture.
description: A former Keystone Cop who directed comedies and dramas for RKO and Paramount, including Cimarron and I'm No Angel with Mae West.

name: Edmund Goulding
signature: Directed Grand Hotel and its star ensemble.
description: An English-born writer and director at MGM and Warner Bros., known for star melodramas: Grand Hotel, Dark Victory with Bette Davis, and the noir Nightmare Alley.

name: Robert Z. Leonard
signature: Directed The Great Ziegfeld, a three-hour musical biography.
description: An MGM house director for three decades, of musicals and costume pictures such as The Great Ziegfeld, Maytime and Pride and Prejudice.

name: Laurence Olivier
signature: The actor who filmed Shakespeare: Henry V, Hamlet and Richard III.
description: The leading stage actor of his generation, he directed and starred in three Shakespeare films, using voice-over soliloquies, deep-focus sets and stylised colour.

name: Michael Anderson
signature: Directed The Dam Busters and Around the World in 80 Days.
description: An English director of war films, spectacles and science fiction, from The Dam Busters to Around the World in 80 Days and Logan's Run.

name: Norman Jewison
signature: Directed In the Heat of the Night and Moonstruck.
description: A Canadian who moved from television to features and made films about racism and justice alongside musicals and comedies, from In the Heat of the Night to Fiddler on the Roof and Moonstruck.

name: Hugh Hudson
signature: Directed Chariots of Fire and its slow-motion run along the beach.
description: A director of commercials who made Chariots of Fire, about two British runners at the 1924 Olympics, then Greystoke and Revolution.

name: Bruce Beresford
signature: A leader of the Australian New Wave who made Breaker Morant and Driving Miss Daisy.
description: Made his name with Australian films such as The Getting of Wisdom and Breaker Morant, then worked in Hollywood on Tender Mercies and Driving Miss Daisy.

name: John Madden
signature: Directed Shakespeare in Love.
description: A British director from theatre and television whose films include Mrs Brown, Shakespeare in Love and The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel.

name: Rob Marshall
signature: A Broadway choreographer who directed the film of Chicago.
description: A stage director and choreographer whose Chicago stages its songs as the heroine's fantasies, followed by Nine, Into the Woods and Mary Poppins Returns.

name: Paul Haggis
signature: Wrote Million Dollar Baby and directed Crash.
description: A Canadian television writer who wrote Million Dollar Baby for Clint Eastwood and directed Crash, an ensemble film about racial tension in Los Angeles.

name: Ben Affleck
signature: Directed Gone Baby Gone, The Town and Argo.
description: An actor who co-wrote Good Will Hunting with Matt Damon, then directed crime films set in Boston, and Argo.

name: Tom McCarthy
signature: Directed The Station Agent and Spotlight.
description: An actor who made quiet independent films about lonely people, such as The Station Agent and The Visitor, then Spotlight, about the Boston Globe's investigation of abuse in the Catholic Church.

name: Peter Farrelly
signature: Co-directed Dumb and Dumber and There's Something About Mary, then made Green Book.
description: With his brother Bobby he made broad comedies in the 1990s, from Dumb and Dumber to There's Something About Mary; alone he directed Green Book.

name: Sian Heder
signature: Wrote and directed CODA.
description: A writer for Orange Is the New Black who directed Tallulah and CODA, about the only hearing member of a deaf fishing family in Massachusetts.

name: Maurice Cloche
signature: Directed Monsieur Vincent, honoured by the Academy in 1949.
description: A French director of religious and social dramas whose Monsieur Vincent, about Saint Vincent de Paul, received an honorary Oscar.

name: Hiroshi Inagaki
signature: Directed the Samurai Trilogy with Toshiro Mifune as Musashi.
description: A director of period films for four decades, best known abroad for his colour Samurai Trilogy about the swordsman Miyamoto Musashi.

name: Serge Bourguignon
signature: Directed Sundays and Cybèle.
description: A French documentary maker whose first feature, Sundays and Cybèle, about a shell-shocked veteran's friendship with a girl, won the Oscar; he then made The Reward in Hollywood.

name: Ján Kadár & Elmar Klos
signature: Made The Shop on Main Street, set in a Slovak town as its Jews are deported.
description: A Slovak-Czech directing partnership of the 1950s and 1960s; in The Shop on Main Street a carpenter is appointed 'Aryan controller' of an old Jewish widow's button shop.

name: Sergei Bondarchuk
signature: Directed the seven-hour War and Peace with vast battle scenes.
description: An actor who directed Fate of a Man and then a four-part War and Peace, with battle scenes using thousands of soldiers, followed by Waterloo.

name: Jean-Jacques Annaud
signature: Made Quest for Fire, The Name of the Rose and The Bear.
description: A French director of large international productions, often set far from the present: prehistory in Quest for Fire, a medieval abbey in The Name of the Rose, animals in The Bear.

name: Moshé Mizrahi
signature: Directed Madame Rosa with Simone Signoret.
description: A Moroccan-born Israeli director who worked in Israel and France; his Madame Rosa, from Romain Gary's novel, stars Simone Signoret as an old woman raising other people's children in Belleville.

name: Vladimir Menshov
signature: Directed Moscow Does Not Believe in Tears.
description: An actor-director whose Moscow Does Not Believe in Tears, following three women from the late 1950s to the late 1970s, was one of the most watched Soviet films.

name: István Szabó
signature: Directed Mephisto with Klaus Maria Brandauer.
description: Hungary's best-known director abroad, whose films, from Father to Mephisto and Colonel Redl, ask how individuals compromise with power.

name: José Luis Garci
signature: Directed To Begin Again, Spain's first Oscar winner for foreign-language film.
description: A Spanish critic and director of nostalgic, classical dramas in the manner of old Hollywood; To Begin Again follows a Nobel laureate returning to his home town of Gijón.

name: Richard Dembo
signature: Directed Dangerous Moves, about a world chess championship.
description: A French director whose first feature, Dangerous Moves, sets a Cold War chess championship in Geneva; it was entered for the Oscar by Switzerland.

name: Luis Puenzo
signature: Directed The Official Story, about a child stolen under the dictatorship.
description: An Argentine director of commercials whose The Official Story, made just after military rule ended, follows a teacher who suspects her adopted daughter was taken from a disappeared prisoner.

name: Fons Rademakers
signature: Directed The Assault, from Harry Mulisch's novel.
description: The leading Dutch director of the 1950s and 1960s, who later adapted Harry Mulisch's The Assault, about a boy whose family is shot in reprisal in 1945, over four decades of his life.

name: Gabriel Axel
signature: Directed Babette's Feast.
description: A Danish director raised in Paris; Babette's Feast, from Karen Blixen's story, ends with a French chef cooking one lavish dinner for an austere Jutland congregation.

name: Xavier Koller
signature: Directed Journey of Hope, about Kurdish migrants crossing the Alps.
description: A Swiss director whose Journey of Hope, based on a real case, follows a Kurdish family from Turkey trying to cross into Switzerland over a mountain pass.

name: Gabriele Salvatores
signature: Directed Mediterraneo.
description: An Italian director from experimental theatre whose Mediterraneo follows Italian soldiers stranded on a Greek island in the Second World War; he later made I'm Not Scared.

name: Régis Wargnier
signature: Directed Indochine with Catherine Deneuve.
description: A French director of romantic historical epics; Indochine follows a French plantation owner and her adopted Vietnamese daughter through the end of colonial rule.

name: Fernando Trueba
signature: Directed Belle Époque and the animated Chico & Rita.
description: A Spanish director and critic of light, music-loving comedies; Belle Époque follows a young deserter and four sisters in 1931, and Chico & Rita is an animated Cuban love story.

name: Nikita Mikhalkov
signature: Directed Burnt by the Sun and An Unfinished Piece for Mechanical Piano.
description: A Russian actor-director of Chekhovian ensemble films and period pieces, from An Unfinished Piece for Mechanical Piano and Oblomov to Burnt by the Sun, about a Red Army hero caught in Stalin's purges.

name: Marleen Gorris
signature: Directed Antonia's Line, the first film by a woman to win the Oscar for foreign-language film.
description: A Dutch feminist director whose debut A Question of Silence follows three women who kill a shopkeeper, and whose Antonia's Line follows four generations of women in a village.

name: Jan Svěrák
signature: Directed Kolya, with his father Zdeněk Svěrák in the lead.
description: A Czech director who often works with his father, the writer and actor Zdeněk Svěrák; Kolya follows a confirmed bachelor left in charge of a Russian boy in 1988 Prague.

name: Mike van Diem
signature: Directed Character, his first feature.
description: A Dutch director whose first feature, Character, tells in flashbacks the long duel between a young clerk in 1920s Rotterdam and the bailiff who is his father.

name: Roberto Benigni
signature: Directed and starred in Life Is Beautiful.
description: A Tuscan comic who directs himself as a manic innocent; in Life Is Beautiful a Jewish father turns life in a concentration camp into a game for his son.

name: Danis Tanović
signature: Directed No Man's Land, set between the lines in the Bosnian war.
description: A Bosnian director who filmed the siege of Sarajevo as a documentarist; No Man's Land traps a Bosnian and a Serb soldier in a trench between the front lines.

name: Caroline Link
signature: Directed Nowhere in Africa.
description: A German director of family dramas; Nowhere in Africa follows a Jewish family that flees Nazi Germany for a farm in Kenya.

name: Denys Arcand
signature: Directed The Decline of the American Empire and The Barbarian Invasions.
description: A Quebec director of talkative, ironic films about Montreal intellectuals, from The Decline of the American Empire to its sequel The Barbarian Invasions, and Jesus of Montreal.

name: Alejandro Amenábar
signature: Directed Open Your Eyes, The Others and The Sea Inside.
description: A Chilean-born Spanish director of psychological thrillers, Thesis, Open Your Eyes and The Others, who then made The Sea Inside, about the paralysed Ramón Sampedro.

name: Gavin Hood
signature: Directed Tsotsi, set in a Johannesburg township.
description: A South African director whose Tsotsi, from Athol Fugard's novel, follows a young gang leader who finds a baby in a car he has stolen; he then made films in Hollywood such as Eye in the Sky.

name: Stefan Ruzowitzky
signature: Directed The Counterfeiters.
description: An Austrian director of genre films whose The Counterfeiters tells the true story of Jewish prisoners forced to forge British pounds in Sachsenhausen.

name: Yōjirō Takita
signature: Directed Departures, about the rituals of preparing the dead.
description: A Japanese director who began in pink films; Departures follows a cellist who loses his orchestra job and becomes a nōkanshi, preparing the dead for cremation.

name: Juan José Campanella
signature: Directed The Secret in Their Eyes, with its long shot into a football stadium.
description: An Argentine director who also works in American television; The Secret in Their Eyes follows a retired court clerk reopening a murder case from the 1970s.

name: Sebastián Lelio
signature: Directed Gloria and A Fantastic Woman.
description: A Chilean director of portraits of women: Gloria, about a divorcée in Santiago, and A Fantastic Woman, about a trans singer facing her late partner's family.

name: Edward Berger
signature: Directed All Quiet on the Western Front (2022) and Conclave.
description: A German director from television whose All Quiet on the Western Front, the first German-language film of Remarque's novel, won four Oscars; he followed it with Conclave.

name: Walter Salles
signature: Directed Central Station, The Motorcycle Diaries and I'm Still Here.
description: A Brazilian director of road movies and family stories, from Central Station and The Motorcycle Diaries to I'm Still Here, about the family of a former congressman taken by the military regime.

name: Wojciech Has
signature: Made The Saragossa Manuscript, a film of stories nested inside stories.
description: A Polish director who turned literary adaptations into dreamlike labyrinths, above all The Saragossa Manuscript, after Jan Potocki, and The Hourglass Sanatorium, after Bruno Schulz.

name: Shane Carruth
signature: Made Primer, a time-travel film shot for about $7,000.
description: An engineer turned film-maker who writes, directs, shoots, scores and acts in his own films; Primer and Upstream Color are known for puzzles they leave unexplained.

name: Martin Rosen
signature: Directed the animated Watership Down and The Plague Dogs.
description: An American producer who directed two bleak animated films from Richard Adams's novels, Watership Down and The Plague Dogs, both made in Britain.

name: Gerald Kargl
signature: Made Angst, a portrait of a killer with a camera that never stops moving.
description: An Austrian director whose only feature, Angst, follows a released prisoner through one day, with Zbigniew Rybczyński's restless camera and the killer's voice-over.

name: Shūji Terayama
signature: A poet and theatre director whose films are psychedelic collages of memory and provocation.
description: A Japanese poet, playwright and founder of the theatre troupe Tenjō Sajiki, whose films, from Throw Away Your Books, Rally in the Streets to Pastoral: To Die in the Country, mix autobiography, street theatre and dream.

name: Dušan Hanák
signature: Made Pictures of the Old World, portraits of old people in Slovak villages.
description: A Slovak director whose documentary Pictures of the Old World portrays elderly villagers of the Carpathians, and whose fiction includes Rosy Dreams and I Love, You Love.

name: Konstantin Lopushansky
signature: A Tarkovsky assistant who made post-apocalyptic visions: Dead Man's Letters and Visitor of a Museum.
description: Worked as an assistant on Tarkovsky's Stalker, then made bleak science-fiction parables about the end of the world, from Dead Man's Letters to Visitor of a Museum.

name: Jonathan Caouette
signature: Made Tarnation from twenty years of home movies, edited in iMovie.
description: An American film-maker and actor whose Tarnation assembles photographs, Super 8 film, answering-machine messages and video diaries into a portrait of his life with his mother.

name: Joaquín Cociña & Cristóbal León
signature: Made The Wolf House, a stop-motion film that seems to be one continuous shot.
description: Two Chilean visual artists who animate paint, papier-mâché and tape in real rooms; The Wolf House draws on Colonia Dignidad, a German sect in Chile.

name: Jack Chambers
signature: A painter whose film The Hart of London collages life and death in his Ontario home town.
description: A Canadian painter of luminous realist landscapes who also made experimental films; The Hart of London assembles archive and home footage of London, Ontario.

name: Peter Tscherkassky
signature: Re-exposes Hollywood frames by hand into found-footage nightmares.
description: An Austrian avant-garde film-maker who copies frames of old films by hand onto new stock in the darkroom; Outer Space and Dream Work rework the horror film The Entity.

name: E. Elias Merhige
signature: Made Begotten, a wordless, grainy creation myth, and Shadow of the Vampire.
description: An American director whose first feature, Begotten, retells a creation myth in harsh black and white without dialogue; he then made Shadow of the Vampire, about the shooting of Nosferatu.
